messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV=P1 - dedicated-pool GPU node failure detected in nimbus-dedicated (VPC). Affected tenant: NimbusCorp (enterprise VPC). Metric: ECC error spike + kernel GPU panic. Auto-evict initiated. Please acknowledge and join #incidents.
raj: acked. I'm oncall SRE. pulling logs now. @miguel can you join for routing/serve-runtime actions? @tara we should loop CS immediately.
miguel: on it. seeing a sequence of AER/ECC errors on gpu-78: kernel log shows repeated nvidia: GPU panic; driver reset; nvlink flaps. Also noticed cloud hint: spot interruption flagged 30s before panic.
sophie: if it's both hw fault and spot notice we need to treat as a hot-preempt + hardware degrade. start tenant isolation now. I'll coordinate drain.
raj: action plan: 1) Isolate node (cordon + taint) 2) Drain active tenants from gpu-78 and route to fallback pool 3) Create temporary dedicated standby (burst) for NimbusCorp if capacity short 4) Notify customer and open ticket 5) HW ops to RMA/replace GPU. Miguel/Tara take points.
miguel: running drain command now: ```
# drain command
rbctl node cordon gpu-78 --pool=nimbus-dedicated
rbctl node taint-add gpu-78 key=dedicated-preempt:NoSchedule
rbctl migrate-tenants --from-node=gpu-78 --to-pool=nimbus-dedicated-fallback --force
``` 
miguel: outputs: migrating 4 tenants (nimbus-api, nimbus-rerank, nimbus-batcher, nimbus-longpoll). Two sessions were active; we are gracefully failing over.
raj: @deploy-bot can you confirm routing policy update completed (canary fallback enabled for tenant routing)?
deploy-bot: routing update: nimbus-tenant -> route priority: [nimbus-dedicated-fallback (100%)]. CDN/session affinity set to allow sticky reattach for 30s.
kev in kevin? Actually participant is kevin; include message
kevin: verified fallback. Performance note: fallback pool uses smaller bfcg quant profile; expect 15-25% latency increase on generation calls.
tara: contacting NimbusCorp now. Notifying that we detected degraded GPU on their dedicated pool, we've moved traffic to fallback pool and are provisioning temporary burst capacity. ETA for replacement/fully restored is ~2 hours (HW verification + node reprovision). Opening support ticket now: INC-98721.
hw-ops: receiving RMA. Can confirm vendor pick-up/remote debug will start once we hand over the node. Please collect nvlog and full kernel oops. We need the PCIe dump and BMC logs.
sophie: grabbing logs: ```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia: GPU0: ECC error threshold exceeded
[ 1234.568000] nvidia: GPU0: pcie AER recovery
[ 1234.570000] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.570400] systemd: service watchdog killed process
``` 
sophie: uploaded /var/log/gpu/gpu-78-evict.log to incident artifacts (s3://redwood-incidents/3501236789/gpu-78-evict.log).
raj: we're seeing 3 active tenants impacted at peak. Customer SLA: 99.9% p95 latency. Tara, do we need to start crediting or offer temporary burst for service degradation?
tara: running initial impact assessment: requests with long-running streams (Nimbus longpoll) had 503s during migration window (approx 18-22s). We're offering a temporary credit and a support call. Notifying account manager.
miguel: mitigation note: enabled prefix/KV cache warmup on fallback pool to reduce token regen cost. Also enabling caching for nimbus-rerank queries.
raj: fallback pool CPU/GPU utilization check: fallback pool nodes at 72% gpu util before migration; after migration peaked at 91% -> we auto-spun a burst node: ```
rbctl pool add-node --pool=nimbus-dedicated-fallback --node-type=gpu-v100-burst --count=1 --labels=temp-burst
``` 
deploy-bot: burst node provisioned and joined pool (node id: gpu-burst-412). Rebalancing tenants.
kevin: confirm we also toggled model variant to quant-qdq to lower memory pressure for rerank under burst. Host fallback model = stable-1.1-qdq.
sophie: double-checking tenant isolation: we set tenant routing tag nimbus:priority=high and pinned to fallback pool until release. Also created a canary policy to fail back only after health checks (10m sustained).
raj: any customer-visible config changes we should announce? e.g., tokenization differences, model variant differences that could affect exact outputs?
kevin: yes — reranks may have slight score variance due to quant profile. Recommend mentioning potential small differences in reranking ordering. For generative output, differences are minimal for short prompts.
tara: NimbusCorp update to customer: "We've detected GPU node failure in your dedicated pool and migrated your traffic to our fallback pool while we replace the node. You may see a small latency increase and minor rerank score variance. We're provisioning temporary burst capacity now. Estimated full restore within 2 hours. Support ticket INC-98721 created." (sent at 11:18 UTC)
raj: handoff plan: I'll stay on for next 45m to ensure stable migration. @sophie please own post-incident RCA and include action items: (1) improve preempt+hw signal correlation to avoid double-failures, (2) verify automigration backoff tuning, (3) run a replay on migration scripts to ensure no 503 windows > 10s.
sophie: taking RCA owner. initial timeline: timeline + logs + mitigation steps will be drafted by EOD. tagging eng-runtime + hw-ops.
miguel: follow-up: we should add a short circuit in routing: if eviction triggered within 60s of spot-notice, prefer immediate migration to fallback before panic to reduce client 503s. I'll open a runtime PR.
raj: final checks: confirm no other dedicated pools impacted. I scanned metrics cluster-wide — no correlated ECC spikes. Marking incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. I'll close page but keep thread open for updates.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: state=MITIGATED, mitigation_time=3501236840, pager_closed_by=raj
tara: closing customer comms loop. CS will follow up with NimbusCorp post-incident summary and credits.
sophie: added RCA owners and initial action list to documented artifacts (s3://redwood-incidents/3501236789/rca.md). Will schedule deep-dive with eng-runtime + hw-ops tomorrow.
raj: thumbs up. If anyone sees re-evict on this node after we eject it, shout here and we'll escalate.
kevin: noting for the runbook: add a step to pre-warm prefix cache on fallback before migration for enterprise tenants.
miguel: PR opened: runtime: add preempt-detection -> preempt-fast-migrate logic (ref: PR#4621).
sophie: assigning postmortem to sophie + miguel. tagging #postmortems when ready.
hw-ops: pickup scheduled at 13:00 UTC. RMA ticket HW-33221.
raj: thanks all. closing this monitoring thread. :white_check_mark:"
